description:
The NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Context Camera (CTX) has captured targeted and serendipitous stereo image data, at 6 meters per pixel spatial resolution across the surface of Mars. This data collection includes Digital Terrain Models (DTMs), at 20 meters per pixel, of stereo image pairs generated using the NASA Ames Stereo Pipeline ([ASP]) (https://github.com/NeoGeographyToolkit/StereoPipeline). DTMs in this collection are aligned to the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), and each DTM has an associated qa_metric.txt file that describes total offsets from MOLA. DTMs are available without any gap filling (for example in crater bottoms). DTMs are GIS ready and elevations values are distance above (or below) the Mars aeroid. Each DTM is presented in a locally centered orthographic projection to minimize distortion. Users can utilize a GIS to reproject these data to a common projection on the fly, work with the local orthographic projection, or use a tool such as [GDAL] (https://gdal.org/) to bulk reproject to another projection (e.g., equirectangular).

MRO CTX stereo images were selected from a subset of CTX images collected concurrently with HiRISE stereo image data acquisition. Data processing occurs in three general phases: (1) ingestion and pre-processing using the USGS Integrated Software for Imagers and Spectrometers ([ISIS]) (https://github.com/USGS-Astrogeology/ISIS3), (2) DTM generation using ASP, and (3) analysis ready data preparation using GDAL. Here, we describe each step in greater detail. First, CTX EDR data are ingested into ISIS using the mroctx2isis application. Then spicefit and spiceinit are run to obtain sensor ephemeris information for each image. Image data are calibrated using ctxcal and detector striping is removed with the evenodd application. In the second phase of the processing pipeline, ASP is used to perform a pairwise bundle adjustment before stereo correlation and point cloud extraction occur. The generated point cloud is aligned to MOLA using pc_align and a DTM is extracted at 20 meters per pixel resolution using point2dem. The DTM is then processed through dem_geoid to obtain heights above the equipotential Mars surface. Finally, ASP generated GeoTiffs are converted to cloud optimized GeoTiffs (COGs) using GDAL.

Fitness of use: Each DTM in this collection includes an associated qa_metric.tx file that reports descriptive statistics describing the [pc_align](https://stereopipeline.readthedocs.io/en/latest/next_steps.html#pc-align-example) computed offsets between the DTM and the MOLA reference. Users should consult both the pc_align documentation, to understand how the rigid transformation is applied to the DTM, and the qa_metrics to determine if the offsets from MOLA are acceptable for their use case. DTMs are provided at a resolution approximately three times the input image spatial resolution. These data are delivered at a spatial resolution that can be expected to be an accurate representation of the topography. The DTMs do not include any hole filling or smoothing. Therefore, we expect artifacts to be present and users should be aware of the effect outlier pixels could have on local scale interpretation.
